Who I Am

Engineering with precision and purpose.

I am a Mechanical Engineer and a recent graduate of the University of Duisburg-Essen with a strong passion for mechanical design, simulation, manufacturing processes, and product development. I am currently enrolled in my M.Sc. Mechanical Engineering at UDE, starting Winter Semester 2026/27.

During my bachelor's thesis, which was awarded a grade of 1.0, I analyzed the influences on roll force, torque, and forward slip in hot flat rolling of steel using fast simulation methods. I completed my B.Sc. with an overall grade of 2.0.

My technical experience includes 3D CAD modeling using SolidWorks (CSWA Certified), Siemens NX, and CATIA V5, FEA with ANSYS, engineering programming using MATLAB/Simulink, and GD&T. I also gained practical industrial experience during my internship at Cairo West Power Station, a 500 MW combined-cycle plant, where I worked on rotating equipment overhaul, hydraulic performance testing, vibration spectrum analysis, and dimensional inspection per DIN EN ISO standards.

I enjoy solving engineering challenges, learning new technologies, and working in collaborative, international environments.

Bachelor Thesis · University of Duisburg-Essen · Grade 1.0 · 2026

Analysis of Influences on Roll Force, Torque and Forward Slip in Hot Flat Rolling of Steel by Fast Simulation

Grade: 1.0ROMICALMATLAB6 Rolling Theories52 Measured Passes5 Parametric Studies

Six analytical rolling theories were evaluated for predicting roll force, torque, and forward slip in hot flat rolling of C55 steel. Each theory was validated against 52 measured passes across five parametric studies.

Study 1 — Effect of Pass Reduction and Roll-Gap Geometry
Investigated how varying pass reduction and roll-gap geometry affects the accuracy of all six theories in predicting rolling force and torque.
Alexander theory: rolling force vs. pass reduction.
Sims theory: rolling force prediction.
Study 2 — Effect of Interstand Tensions
Analyzed the influence of front and back tension between stands on rolling force and torque predictions across three sub-studies.
Tension effect on rolling force.
Tension effect on torque.
Study 3 — Effect of Friction Parameters
Examined how varying friction coefficients influence the prediction accuracy of rolling force, torque, and forward slip.
Friction effect on rolling force.
Friction effect on torque.
Friction effect on forward slip.
Study 4 — Comparison to Measured Data (52 Passes)
Direct validation of all six theories against 52 measured passes. Quantified relative prediction errors to determine which theories perform best.
Rolling force: all theories vs. measurements.
Torque: all theories vs. measurements.
Relative error deltaF per theory.
Study 5 — Warm Strip Rolling in Multi-Stand Configuration
Extended the analysis to a multi-stand warm strip rolling configuration, evaluating theory performance across sequential passes.
Rolling force across stands.
Torque across multiple stands.
